h: A Few More Liverpool Gems to Bolt On
p: If you've done the Albert Dock and the Cavern, there's still plenty more to fill a Liverpool weekend. The Pier Head is home to the Three Graces, including the Royal Liver Building with its famous Liver Birds perched on top. From there, a Mersey Ferry trip across the river is a classic, with brilliant views back to the waterfront skyline.

Up by Lime Street Station, St George's Hall is a magnificent neoclassical building, and right beside it the World Museum and the Walker Art Gallery are both free to visit. The Walker is home to an impressive art collection, and the World Museum is great with kids, from dinosaurs to a planetarium. A wander along Bold Street will sort you out for food, with plenty of independent restaurants and cafés to try before your game.

At the lanes, a little know-how helps. Pick a ball you can swing comfortably rather than the heaviest one going, aim at the arrows on the lane rather than the pins, and keep your arm straight as you release. In bowling, three strikes in a row is a turkey, so if anyone manages it, you have permission to make a lot of noise.
Liverpool gets very busy on football weekends and around big events, so check what's on before you travel and book your lane, hotel and table for food well in advance.
